subject: laserbeam
label: sprites/laserbeam.spr, in the place of the game's own

R1.reason: The frame reads as a laser beam: a narrow vertical strip running the full height of the frame, a white-hot core down the middle (x about 55 to 70 of the 128-px picture) and a blue glow falling off to each side. The brief's core-plus-glow description is met. The picture is small, so fine glow falloff can only be judged coarsely.

R2.reason: The 64x32 frame is filled as a beam fills it: the strip runs edge to edge top to bottom (border max 0.978) and the rest is dark (dark 0.71), with no stray marks beyond the harness's frame-number box at top left. The measures give no class comparison (againstClass is empty), so the size itself is not checked against Half-Life's own beams.

R3.reason: Colours match the brief: a near-white core at the centre, blue falling to darker blue at the sides, on black, which additive blending suits. Nothing was measured against an original's mean colour, so this is judged by eye.

R4.reason: The sprite is a single frame (frames 1, first and last 1, peak at 0), which suits a steady beam. But no class comparison was made, so the frame count of Half-Life's own beam sprites is unknown and the frame count cannot be shown to be within 25% of it.

R5.reason: The type (parallel) and format (additive) match the original's (gameType parallel, gameFormat additive). The name is the same (sameName true) and the file reads back as written (readsBack true).
